entry.title: macOS buttons have come a long way. See the 40-year evolution here
entry.content:
Macworld

The Mac operating system has been around for over 42 years, and it’s seen a lot of changes. There’s one aspect of the user interface that has changed a lot: the buttons that appear on screen. Button changes usually accompany major graphical overhauls, so they’re easy to overlook.

Now there’s a website that has collected them all in a neat interactive gallery. At mac-buttons-timeline.vercel.app, the different button styles can be viewed by scrolling along a Time Machine-esque timeline. Turns out that over 42 years, there have been 11 different style changes.

By looking at the different designs, you can see that Apple has gone back and forth between more elaborate designs to very simple ones. You have the bold original button from 1984, which transitioned to a very simple button in 1986. That button stuck around for 11 years until Apple gave it a shade of gray in 1997. Then there were the glossy, gradient days of Mac OS X Aqua in the early and mid 2000s, before Apple shifted back to more simpler buttons again.

The timeline is a fun trip through a part of the Mac operating system that isn’t usually given much thought. The next time you click “OK,” know that there’s someone who has put a lot of thought into that button.

entry.title: Wait, is the iPhone 18 Pro really faster than an M4 Mac?
entry.content:
Macworld

You’re not going to want to believe this. It doesn’t feel like it should be true. But it is: The A20 Pro in the iPhone 18 Pro is legitimately faster than a standard M4 as found in the recent Mac mini, or current iMac.

That’s right. Faster. And not just “sort of faster in just this one test when you run in one specific way.” Faster overall. Faster generally.

Yes, of course there are caveats, and we’ll get to those. But as defensible claim, we can say that Apple’s advancements in chip design and manufacturing processes have now made the iPhone in your pocket faster than the entry-level desktop computers they were selling just two years ago. Crazy, right?

CPU performance

If there’s a place to equivocate about a “faster” claim, it’s in the CPU performance. Let’s take a look at Geekbench 6 and Geekbench 7 numbers. The M4 numbers here are from a Mac mini with the full 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU.

Foundry

Apple called the two big super cores in the A20 Pro “desktop class” and it’s hard to argue when the single-core performance is 28 percent higher than the M4. But the M4 has 10 cores and the A20 Pro has 6, so it’s just got too big an advantage in multi-core processing. Still, it’s only 13 percent faster despite having more cores to work with.

Foundry

The newer Geekbench 7 scores, with represent more strenuous and modern workloads, tell a similar story. Single-core performance of the little computer in your pocket is 22 percent higher than the bigger computer on your desk. The multi-core benefit of the M4 is about 27 percent here, despite having 67 percent more cores.

So yes, multi-threaded performance and multitasking on the M4 will be faster than the A20 Pro, for tasks that heavily utilize all the CPU cores. But for any task that is limited by the performance of a single thread (which are quite common), the A20 Pro is quite a bit faster than the M4.

GPU performance

Modern computing platforms rely in GPU performance as much as CPU performance, perhaps even more so. Does the M4 hold an advantage there? Nope!

Foundry

The Geekbench GPU compute tests measure the GPU’s ability to do computational tasks like face tracking, image upscaling, or particle physics simulation. Whether it’s the older Geekbench 6 test or the newer Geekbench 7 test, the A20 Pro is 15-28 percent faster than the M4. This is despite only having 7 GPU cores to the M4’s 10 cores, and slightly less memory bandwidth (about 115 GB/s to 120 GB/s). Architectural changes really matter!

For a look at actual 3D graphics rendering performance we’ll turn to 3DMark. Not all these tests are available on the Mac, so for some of these scores we’ll turn to the M4 iPad Pro, using the same 10/10 core configuration as the Mac mini.

Foundry

The most strenuous test with no ray-tracing, Steel Nomad Light, is a tie. For everything else, the A20 Pro is significantly faster. Solar Bay Unlimited, which has significant ray tracing demands, is 19% faster on the mobile chip. The older Wild Life Extreme Unlimited test, which uses older graphics techniques and no ray tracing, is still just slightly faster (8%) on the A20 Pro.

It’s kind of crazy. Apple’s new iPhone chip, with 7 GPU cores and ~115 GB/s of memory bandwidth, is outclassing its entry-level desktop chip from two years ago despite the fact that it has 10 GPU cores and ~120 GB/s of memory bandwidth. This is for both compute and 3D graphics rendering.

AI performance

There aren’t a lot of good AI tests for both mobile and desktop, but the Geekbench AI suite lets us run through a bunch of AI/ML inferencing tasks using the CPU, GPU, or Neural Engine.

Foundry

Apple doubled the Neural Engine in the A20 Pro (and M6) to 32 cores, and it really pays off. Single-precision workloads are more than 30 percent faster, and half-precision or quantized tasks (most common for consumer AI applications) are 53 percent faster.

That’s about 50 percent higher AI performance on the latest iPhone compared to a Mac mini or iMac from just two years ago.

But not all AI workloads run only on dedicated neural processing units. It’s common for GPU hardware to work on AI tasks, so let’s see what happens when we run the same tests using the GPU.

Foundry

It’s a bloodbath. Single-precision tasks are “only” 15 percent higher, but half-precision task are a whopping 84 percent faster using the A20 Pro’s GPU than the M4’s GPU. Quantized operations are more than twice as fast—116 percent faster to be exact!

Apple added hardware to the GPU cores to specifically accelerate AI tasks in the A19 Pro and M5 generation, and of course that carries onto the A20 Pro. They obviously make a huge difference, because you’re seeing less cores and memory bandwidth on the iPhone 18 Pro deliver twice the performance as an M4 Mac.

The fine print

While it’s entirely defensible to call the A20 Pro “faster than the M4,” and we have the receipts to prove it, we’d be remiss not to mention a few caveats.

First, the Macs and iPhones have different operating systems that are made to be used differently, so your actual productivity on an M4 Mac won’t be lower just because the chip has lower benchmark scores. Also, nearly any Mac will have better cooling performance than an iPhone 18 Pro. So while these benchmarks are accurate for short bursts of performance, you can put your thumb on the scale in favor of the M4 Mac for long tasks where things get hot (though we still imagine the iPhone 18 Pro would win in many cases).

And finally, we’re not comparing Apple’s latest iPhone chip to its latest Mac chip. The M4 was first introduced about two years ago, in late 2024. But until just recently, the M4 was the entry-level chip for the Mac mini. It only just got replaced in the Mac mini and it’s still the only chip you can get in an iMac.

Just imagine what a MacBook Neo would be like with an A20 Pro inside. We suspect that laptop will be updated in 2027, but it will probably get an A19 Pro, as the current model has an A18 Pro. That means an A20 Pro-packing MacBook Neo isn’t likely to happen until 2028.

entry.title: My Apple Watch Series 12 lasted over 2X longer than Apple says
entry.content:
Macworld

When reviewing the Apple Watch Series 11 last year, I found the battery performance across multiple complete power drain tests to be nothing less than superb. In fact, that’s the exact word I used.

Last year, Apple bumped up the estimated life to 24 hours (after holding steady at 18 hours for the previous 10 generations), and our testing more than justified this ambitious claim. In fact, real-world performance seemed roughly double that: In one test, the Series 11 lasted for 46 hours, and 49 in another. In both cases it managed a day, a night, another day, and then most or all of another night; the only question was how far it would make it into the morning of the third day. Impressive stuff.

With such high standards to live up to, I wasn’t sure what to expect from the Apple Watch Series 12, which I’m currently testing for an upcoming review. Officially it’s rated with the same estimate as its predecessor: up to 24 hours. Unofficially, I took note of the inclusion of continual heart-rate monitoring as the headline new feature and wondered how much of an impact this would have on battery performance. I was prepared for a dip in last year’s numbers that were still ahead of Apple’s estimates.

The impact of the new sensor, it appears, is not very much. Either that, or the new S11 processor has such a positive impact that it more than cancels out the energy burden of the health feature.

I’ve just completed my first complete battery test of the Series 12, and it lasted a whopping 51 hours, surpassing both runs of the Series 11 by at least a couple of hours. It lasted two full days, two full nights, and made it to mid-morning on the third day. By the standards of a fully featured smartwatch, that’s elite performance.

There are caveats, of course. This is only my first test, and I plan to run at least one more complete power-down before committing my thoughts to a full review. Battery performance is in any case quite subjective: there’s no established battery benchmark app as there is for the iPhone or the Mac, and battery life will vary based on usage. And on the negative side, my first charging test of the Series 12 suggests it powers up more slowly than its predecessor, requiring 57 minutes to get from 0 to 80 percent, compared to just 40 minutes for the Series 11. (Again, I plan to run this test again for reliability.)

Still, the early signs are that the Apple Watch Series 12 has managed to take one of the highlights of the Series 11 and surpass it. This is a promising start, to say the least.

entry.title: Create a Custom Pass in the Wallet App on iPhone
entry.content:
In iOS 27, Apple's Wallet app lets you create custom passes for things like event tickets, gift cards, loyalty cards, and more. Here's how it works.


If you have a ticket for an event and there's not a digital version available for the Wallet app, you can create one using the physical pass you have. The same goes for other cards, like a membership card, for example.

The Wallet app can use ‌Visual Intelligence‌ to scan your card, and it will match it to a template with corresponding fields that you can tweak before adding it to your Wallet.

Alternatively, you can create the pass manually, choose a template ("Membership," "Event," or "Custom") and then adjust the color and other details. All you need to do then is scan the barcode or QR code from your physical pass.

Each template includes relevant information like name, location, or admission type. There are 12 background colors to choose from, or seven custom backgrounds for categories like theater, music, sports, and movies.

Fields can be added or removed when creating a custom pass, with options like label, date, membership, contact, coupon code, VIN, insurance, and more, so most physical cards should be able to be stored digitally.

Here's how you create a pass with ‌Visual Intelligence‌:
  1. Open the Wallet app on your iPhone and tap the + button at the top.

  2. Choose Create a Pass.

  3. To let Visual Intelligence scan the pass, tap Continue, then take a photo of it in the next screen.

  4. After Visual Intelligence matches the pass to a template, tap Edit Pass.

  5. Use the palette icon in the bottom-left corner to change the look of the pass – you can the background colour, or use an image from your Photos library. Tap the icon in the bottom-right corner to add or remove fields.

  6. Tap the blue checkmark at the top when you're done.
Your custom pass will now be added to your Wallet, ready for use. To edit it at any time, simply select it in Wallet, tap the three dots in the top-right corner of the screen, then tap Edit Pass.

At $799/£799, the iPhone 17 also compares very favourably with the older iPhone 16. For just $100/£100 more, you get double the base storage, ProMotion, a larger and brighter display, improved cameras, the newer A19 chip and significantly better battery life.

If your priority is spending as little as possible, choose the iPhone 17e which delivers excellent performance for $599/£599. Or seek out a refurbished iPhone from the Apple Refurbished Store or another place that sells refurbished iPhones.

Our choice: In terms of the features and hardware you get for every pound or dollar spent, the iPhone 17 is the sweet spot. For most buyers, it delivers the best balance of price, performance, cameras, display quality, battery life and longevity without paying for Pro-level features they may never use. Even better if you can find a iPhone 17 deal, then you are really getting a bargain.

Best iPhone for gaming: iPhone 18 Pro

Foundry

The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone for gaming for most people, thanks to its combination of the A20 Pro chip, seven-core GPU and improved vapor-chamber cooling.

The A20 Pro is Apple’s fastest iPhone processor, but the cooling system is just as important for gaming. Better heat management should help the iPhone 18 Pro maintain high performance for longer during demanding games, rather than slowing down as the phone gets hot. Its 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display also provides smooth animation and responsive gameplay without making the phone excessively large or heavy.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers essentially the same gaming performance, but adds a much larger 6.9-inch display and significantly longer battery life. That arguably makes it the best choice for serious mobile gamers who value screen size and endurance, although it is heavier and costs more.

The iPhone Duo also uses the A20 Pro and has an enormous 7.6-inch folding display, which could be fantastic for some games, but its weight, price and unconventional form factor make it a more specialised choice.

Our choice: For most gamers, the iPhone 18 Pro offers the best balance of performance, cooling, display quality and portability. It’s the best choice if you prefer a more pocketable device but still want top-tier gaming power.

Best iPhone for seniors and older users: iPhone 17e

David Price / Foundry

For most older users, the iPhone 17e is probably the best choice, because it combines a relatively simple feature set with modern performance, strong battery life and a lower price than Apple’s flagship models.

Its 6.1-inch OLED display is large enough to make text, icons and controls easy to see without making the phone too bulky, while the A19 chip should keep it feeling fast for years. It also supports Apple Intelligence and starts with 256GB of storage, so there’s plenty of room for photos, apps and videos.

The iPhone 17 is a better option for someone who would benefit from a larger and more advanced display. Its 6.3-inch ProMotion screen, Always-On support and higher brightness can make scrolling, reading and outdoor use more comfortable. It also offers stronger battery life and better cameras, although it costs more.

We don’t recommend the iPhone Air, Pro Max or Duo for older users. The Air sacrifices battery life and camera flexibility for thinness, while the Pro Max and Duo are much heavier and considerably more expensive.

Our choice: iPhone 17e is the perfect choice for most older users.

Best iPhone for kids: iPhone 17e

Ida Blix

The iPhone 17e is the best iPhone for most children. As Apple’s most affordable current-generation model, it offers the best balance of price, performance and longevity, while being easier to justify than a flagship model if it gets lost or damaged.

It uses the same A19 chip as the iPhone 17, albeit with one fewer GPU core, so it’s easily fast enough for games, social media, schoolwork and Apple Intelligence. Battery life is strong, the 6.1-inch OLED display is a sensible size for smaller hands, and the 48MP camera is more than capable for everyday photos, even though it lacks an Ultra Wide lens.

The iPhone 17 is the better choice for older teenagers who care more about photography, video or display quality. It adds a 48MP Ultra Wide camera, a better front camera and a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion display, but costs considerably more.

A hand-me-down iPhone is also worth considering. It’s the cheapest option and better for the environment, provided you erase the phone first, create a Child Account through Family Sharing, and configure Screen Time and parental controls before handing it over. Read: How to set up an iPhone for a child.

Whichever iPhone you choose, those controls matter. In iOS 27, Apple is expanding Screen Time with new category-based Time Allowances, Ask to Browse, more flexible app schedules and improved contact controls. Communication Safety can also detect and blur sensitive, violent or graphic content.

For very young children, an iPad may still be a better first Apple device. By the time they reach 11 or 12 though, an iPhone becomes much more useful for staying in touch.

Our choice: iPhone 17e for most kids; iPhone 17 for older teens who want better cameras and display quality.

Should you buy an older iPhone?

Macwelt

Buying an older iPhone can be a great way to save money, but the key is choosing a model that still has plenty of useful life ahead of it. Apple typically provides around five to seven years of major iOS updates, with security updates often continuing for longer, so a relatively recent iPhone can remain perfectly usable for years.

We wouldn’t recommend simply buying the cheapest iPhone you can find. Very old models may technically run recent versions of iOS, but performance, battery condition and access to newer features can become increasingly compromised. We currently recommend avoiding anything older than the iPhone 15 Pro because even the iPhone 15 doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. You should definitely avoid models such as the iPhone XS and XR that can no longer run the latest iOS releases.

A refurbished recent-generation iPhone can offer particularly good value. You may be able to buy a former Pro model with better cameras and displays for less than a new entry-level iPhone. Buying from a reputable refurbisher is important, however: check the warranty, battery condition, returns policy and whether genuine replacement parts have been used. Apple’s own refurbished iPhones include a new battery and outer shell and come with a one-year warranty.

Our advice: A discounted or refurbished iPhone 16 or newer should offer an excellent combination of price, features and longevity.

entry.title: Your iPhone camera is great. These accessories will make it even better
entry.content:
Macworld

I used to carry around my trusted Canon 350D camera everywhere. But these days, I don’t need a bulky DSLR to capture beautiful photos. I just use my iPhone.

But even the best iPhone camera has its limitations. A good accessory can help you get steadier video, better sound, more flattering lighting, specialist lens effects or simply a more comfortable grip when you’re shooting for long periods. And if you want to take your iPhone underwater or turn it into a more serious video rig, the right add-ons can make an even bigger difference.

If you’re like me and are more than happy shooting with the iPhone, you might be looking for some tip-top extras to make the process even more rewarding.

And that’s where we come in, as the curated list below is stacked with iPhone accessories designed to elevate your smartphone snaps and videos. Let’s see what’s in store.

Moment lenses

Moment

Apple’s iPhone cameras are superb when it comes to their image quality, especially on the latest models. But even Apple’s best lack some of the range and features you’ll find in dedicated SLR lenses. How do you go about getting the best of both worlds? With some of Moment’s iPhone lenses.

Moment makes all sorts of specialist lenses for a range of iPhone models. You’ll find everything from close-up macro options to cinematic anamorphic lenses, with plenty of choices available to fit your needs. Just ensure you pick up a compatible case or mounting system and you’ll be good to go. Check out Moment’s Mobile Lens Store at Amazon.

ShiftCam ProGrip

ShiftCam

It’s surprisingly easy to fumble your iPhone when you’re trying to line up the perfect shot, especially if you’re in the middle of the action and everything is moving quickly. To ensure you don’t miss out on that unique moment, consider getting one of ShiftCam’s ProGrip attachments.

This adds an SLR-style hand grip and trigger button to your iPhone setup. It holds your iPhone in place (landscape or portrait) while giving you a rock-solid grasp when shooting. It also makes it much easier to snap your photos one-handed and even has a built-in power bank to keep you going on long shoots. See the ShiftCam ProGrip on Amazon.

SmallRig All-in-One Video Kit for Smartphone Creators

SmallRig

For more control over your iPhone photography and filming work, it’s worth investing in a two-handed grip. One of the best is the SmallRig All-In-One Kit for Smartphone ($189 on Amazon), and it really is just about all you need for this sort of work.

Here, you’ll find two sturdy hand grips, a 360-degree tripod, a cardioid microphone, cold shoes and holders for attaching accessories like flashes and battery packs, and all the cables you need to get started. If you’ve ever thought about doing some serious shooting with your iPhone, it’s a great piece of kit to have.

SeaLife SportDiver Ultra

SeaLife

Modern iPhones have a degree of water resistance these days, but you shouldn’t rely on its built-in protection for serious underwater photography. Instead, you need a proper waterproof case.

A good example is the SeaLife SportDiver Ultra ($349 on Amazon). It’s certified for use down to depths of 130 feet (40 meters), giving you peace of mind that it can hold its own on the vast majority of dives. There’s an included color correction filter to ensure everything looks as it should, while its anti-fogging capsule keeps your pictures clear and moisture-free. It’s also designed to be easy to hold and use, even when you’re wearing diving gloves.

Insta360 Flow 2

Insta360

Tired of shaky photos and videos? You need a gimbal. One of your best options is the Insta360 Flow 2 ($110 on Amazon), a phone holder that can keep your device stable and level, and make wobbly results a thing of the past.

This model features three-axis stabilization for ultimate smoothness, a built-in selfie stick, tripod and power bank, and a smartphone remote control. On the software side, you get zoom and multi-person tracking to keep your subjects in the frame at all times, and you can even use your Apple Watch as a trigger and framing device. It’s a good choice if action shots are your bread and butter.

DJI Mic 3

DJI

Whether you’re conducting interviews or recording yourself for social media, a dedicated microphone can give you much better results than just using the one included in your iPhone. But there’s no need to get a big, bulky mic that’s a pain to lug around. Buy the DJI Mic 3 instead ($259 on Amazon).

It’s easy to get started thanks to its magnetic clip that lets you attach it to any piece of clothing. With two levels of active noise cancelation, your recordings should be well protected against external distractions, and its software-integrated timecode and support for 32-bit float make it an attractive option for video editors. It’s the type of accessory that performs far beyond what you’d expect from its pocketable frame.

ShiftCam SnapStudio Light

ShiftCam

The nighttime performance of Apple’s cameras has come on leaps and bounds in recent years, but you’ll still find scenarios where it falls a little short. For times like that, the ShiftCam SnapStudio Light ($89 on Amazon) can be a lifesaver.

This light rig snaps onto your iPhone’s MagSafe point and delivers up to 600 lumens of brightness, illuminating you without washing out the picture, and with an adjustable color temperature ranging from 2500K to 6000K, you’re always in control. There’s also a built-in grip that doubles up as a tripod, and you can flip the light through 180 degrees for picture-perfect selfies.

Polaroid Hi·Print 4×6 Photo Printer

Polaroid

What’s the fun of taking all these great photos on your iPhone if they stay confined to your device? Part of the joy is printing them out so you can frame them or share them with friends, which is exactly what you get with the Polaroid Hi·Print 4×6 Photo Printer ($149 on Amazon).

This nifty little product prints out your photos in the popular 4×6-inch format, giving you a new way to enjoy your snaps in just a few seconds. All you need to do is connect your iPhone to the Polaroid Hi-Print app and load the printer up with compatible paper, then you’re on your way. You can add text, frames, emojis and more to your images, or just print them as they are. Either way, it’s a neat way to enjoy a touch of print-out photo physicality the retro way.

Don’t sleep on the App Store

You don’t always need to buy an accessory to have a better time shooting photos and videos on your iPhone. In fact, some of the best extras are included for free inside iOS.

Take portrait mode, for example, which adds beautiful depth-of-field effects that can be edited after the fact. If you have an Apple Watch, you can use it as a remote shutter for your iPhone, perfect for family group shots. And iOS 27 now includes advanced AI editing tools.

If you want to look outside Apple’s walled garden, there is a mature ecosystem of pro-grade photo and video apps ready to explore. That includes the likes of Halide, (Not Boring) Camera, CapCut, Blackmagic Camera, and many more.

Our Verdict

The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro delivered excellent results in our battery tests and combines fast 25W wireless charging with active cooling, 45W USB-C and an excellent adjustable kickstand. It’s chunkier and pricier than some 10K rivals, and lacks a built-in cable, but it’s one of the most capable magnetic power banks we’ve tested.

What is it? A fast, high-capacity power bank with active cooling that magnetically connects to your iPhone for 25W wireless charging with an extra USB-C port for wired power output/input.

Who is it for? Owners of the iPhone 16/17/18 will get the full benefit of the 25W wireless charging.

Who shouldn’t buy it? Older iPhones (iPhone 15 and earlier) that have wireless charging limited to 15W.

Although reserved for only iPhones 16 and later, 25W is now the de facto speed for magnetic power banks. There are still plenty of excellent 15W wireless portable chargers but if you can upgrade to 25W it’ll mean faster wireless charging when you do trade up to a newer iPhone if you haven’t already.

The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro is a solid 10000mAh magnetic wireless portable charger with a built-in kickstand and what Anker calls an “ultra-wide air inlet” that’s larger than I’ve seen previously on any power bank. Behind the air inlet’s dual air channels is an active cooling fan.

25W wireless charging creates a lot of heat that can force an iPhone into a self-safety mode that throttles the amount of power going into it or even stops it altogether. That’s why cooling is so important with this level of charger power.

In our tests, the MagGo 2 Pro charged an iPhone 16 Pro to 50% in 30 minutes with active cooling enabled, compared to 33 minutes in Silent Mode. It also delivered 199% total charge in our capacity test, comfortably beating the 174% average for 10K power banks we’ve tested.

Power bank specs

  • Capacity: 39.2Wh (10000mAh)
  • Input charger: USB-C (45W)
  • Output charger: Wireless (25W) & USB-C (45W)
  • On test charged iPhone to: 199%
  • Weight: 7.76oz (220g)
  • Dimensions: 4.1 x 2.8 x 0.7 inches (105 x 71 x 17.8mm)
  • Colors: Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, Starlight Silver

What is the exact battery capacity of the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro?

Although we’ve seen some larger, 10000mAh (10K milliamp hours) is the largest battery size that you can clamp to the back of your MagSafe iPhone without it being too cumbersome to pocket or just fall off through its own bulk. Smaller pockets will appreciate a smaller 5000mAh (5K) power bank. Read reviews of all the best magnetic power banks we have tested, both 5K and 10K.

While it’s industry standard to talk of “5K” and “10K” power banks, it should be noted that not all in each of these broad categories have exactly the same actual capacity. To be more precise you need to look at the battery capacity in watt hours (Wh) rather than milliamp hours (mAh). The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro’s 39.2Wh is higher than the average 10K battery capacity of 38.2Wh.

Simon Jary

How fast is the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro?

For wireless power output the MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro is rated at the top 25W, using the fastest Qi2.2 technology. Only the iPhone 16 series and later can take all 25W of this power output, with older iPhones pegged back at 15W (still much faster than the 7.5W still offered by some battery packs). Note that the 17e is also limited to 15W, and the iPhone Air to 20W. If you own the iPhone 16e you’re out of luck as that curiously doesn’t support MagSafe charging.

In our tests the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro recharged our test iPhone 16 Pro to 50% in 30 minutes, which is what we’d expect from a 25W charger, and much faster than the average 45 minutes it would take with a 15W wireless charger. It rates as a couple of minutes faster than the average, although environmental factors have a large impact—mainly from heat. Later, we’ll look at how Anker’s smart fan impacts charging times.

The MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro’s sole USB-C port is rated at 45W so will charge your iPhone much faster than wireless if you need to power up as quickly as possible, but you’ll need to bring a USB-C cable as it doesn’t come with its own built-in as you find on some power banks. In the box there is a separate 1ft (0.3m) USB-C to USB-C cable (plus a soft storage pouch) but it isn’t integrated into the portable charger.

Simon Jary

45W USB-C, also found on the Ugreen MagFlow Pro and Baseus PicoGo AM52, is the fastest we’ve seen on a magnetic power bank. Previously, we’d have said this was overkill for an iPhone but Apple now states that the iPhone 17 series can wired-charge up to 50% charge in 20 minutes using a 40W charger, and only 15 minutes using a 60W charger for the latest iPhone 18 Pro.

It’s also a handy power delivery if you are charging an iPad and even a MacBook Neo or Air.

Input: When recharging the power bank itself, the power input is 45W—one of the fastest you’ll find on any magnetic wireless power bank range. That should mean that you can recharge the power bank to 80% in less than an hour—handy for those times you’ve forgotten to charge the power bank before heading out.

Simon Jary

Is active cooling better than passive?

25W delivers nearly 70% more power than legacy 15W charging, which can lead to thermal buildup that triggers speed throttling and even impact long‑term battery health.

The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro has two charging modes, which you activate with the charging button while looking at the display.

Silent Mode is without the fan on, and Cool Mode is with the fan working. The ultra-wide air inlet no doubt allows for some passive cooling, and we achieved a 50% charge in 33 minutes compared to the faster 30 minutes with the fan on. Depending on the heat you are charging in, this difference may be extended in your circumstances.

While it will charge your iPhone faster in Cool mode, the MagGo 2 Pro’s fan is audible close up. We’ve heard louder fans on power banks, such as the Ugreen MagFlow Pro Magnetic Power Bank, and if it’s placed a short distance away from you it shouldn’t disturb you, but you wouldn’t want it purring away on your nightstand while you try to sleep—although you won’t need the speedier charging if doing it overnight anyway.

Simon Jary

How well does the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro’s battery perform?

At Macworld we produce a battery performance report for all the power banks that pass through our labs.

We simply drain an iPhone’s battery to 0%, connect the power bank and see how many times it can recharge the phone from the moment the Apple logo shows up. A 10K power bank will be able to do this more than once before being completely drained itself, so we wait till the phone has run out again and repeat until the power bank is empty.

The best score we have got from a 10000mAh (10K) power bank is 207% (the 25W Ugreen MagFlow Pro), with an average score across all 10K portable chargers of 174%. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro scored an impressive and well-above-average 199%—not far off the Ugreen, and again environmental factors can impact performance.

Simon Jary

What’s special about the MagGo 2 Pro’s design?

The MagGo 2 Pro isn’t the slimmest 10K power bank we’ve tested. That honor goes to Kuxiu S4 25W Semi-Solid Wireless 10K Power Bank at just 0.53 inches (13.7mm) thick. The Anker power bank is noticeably chunkier at 0.7 inches (17.8mm) but it’s not semi-solid-state like the S4.

It’s a little shorter but deeper than the 10K Ugreen MagFlow Pro, which measures 4.3 x 2.8 x 0.63 inches (108 x 71 x 16mm), but fractionally lighter at 220g vs 235g, although that extra is the Ugreen’s integrated USB-C cable—a feature lacking from the Anker.

It does have a sturdy kickstand with 0-80° adjustment, as does the Kuxiu S4 but not the Ugreen. This means you can prop your iPhone up either vertically or horizontally for easy viewing or StandBy Mode when charging.

Simon Jary

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro has an informative digital display on one side, showing you how much power remains in the power bank as a precise percentage rather than the standard power bank four tiny LEDs. You can tap through six screens to check charging status, battery level, battery health, and temperature, or quickly switch Silent and Cool charging modes and wireless charging on or off. Anker has made the display larger than most other power bank makers so it is clear and easy to read, as well as operate.

Anker

In terms of colors, the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro is available in four: Burgundy Red to match the newest iPhone color, Polar Night Blue for Glacier, plus Starlight Silver and Phantom Gray for the Silver and Black iPhones.

Of course, the Anker MagGo 2 Pro works with older iPhones, too: any model after iPhone 12 except the poor MagSafe-less 16e.

Anker

If you want a different color but similar power bank check out Anker’s older 15W MagGo Power Bank (10K) that has a display just like the MagGo 2 Pro reviewed here. It’s a little slower (an extra 15 minutes for the iPhone to reach 50%) and scored 170% in our recharge tests, but it does come in more colors (see above) and you might find a bargain on Amazon. We still recommend the newer 25W power bank for its speed, cooling and more informative display.

How much does the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro cost?

The Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro is priced at $109.99 or £99.99, which is at the top end for 10K magnetic wireless portable chargers, but reasonable with the fast charging and above-average performance plus the active cooling option. It is also available from Amazon in all four colors.

For more options we have tested and reviewed the best magnetic wireless power banks.

Simon Jary

Should you buy the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro?

Fast and performing excellently in our battery tests, the Anker MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro is easy to recommend, especially with its adjustable and sturdy kickstand. There are slimmer 10K power banks and ones with built-in cables, but the MagGo 2 Pro is a robust choice for your high-capacity magnetic wireless charger.

entry.title: How to Check Your Mac's Manufacture Date in macOS 27
entry.content:
If you installed macOS 27 Golden Gate, here's a way to find out when your Mac was manufactured. Apple has restored access to information that effectively disappeared when it randomized its serial numbers a few years ago.


On your Mac, go to System Settings ➝ General ➝ About, then click "Regulatory Certification" under the System Report button. The certificate will show with a new "Date of Manufacture" field at the bottom.

You used to be able to decode the serial number on an Apple device to find out when and where it was made. That changed in 2021, when Apple began adopting randomized serial numbers without encoded manufacturing details.

That left owners of newer Macs with no similarly straightforward way to determine when their machine was made – until macOS 27 arrived.


The spot was made by MacRumors forum member pdfu. Another forum member said that the displayed date they saw on their certificate corresponded to their Mac's logic board rather than the date the complete machine was assembled. That logic board had been replaced though, suggesting that's where the date of manufacture is stored.

The regulatory certification first appeared during the macOS 27 beta cycle and it hasn't, to our knowledge, been highlighted by Apple.

entry.title: What's Gone in macOS Golden Gate and What's Next in macOS 28
entry.content:
With macOS Golden Gate, Apple phased out several legacy features and services, cutting support for older devices and accessories. More cuts are coming in macOS 28 as Apple continues to root out lingering Intel features.


Here's everything that's been dropped.

  • Support for Intel Macs - ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ is the first version of macOS that runs only on Apple silicon Macs. Intel Macs can't run it and are limited to macOS Tahoe. Apple still plans to offer security updates through fall 2028.

  • Boot Camp Assistant - Since ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ doesn't run on Intel Macs, it doesn't support Boot Camp. Apple silicon Macs require virtualization software like Parallels or VMware Fusion to run Windows.

  • Rosetta 2 (Temporarily) - Upgrading to ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ removes Rosetta, but if you have an app installed that requires it, you can reinstall it. ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ is the last version of macOS that will have full Rosetta support.

  • Apple Filing Protocol - Apple deprecated AFP back in macOS Sequoia 15.5, and there is no AFP client at all in ‌macOS Golden Gate‌.

  • Time Capsule Backups - With no support for AFP, Time Capsule no longer works with Macs running ‌macOS Golden Gate‌. Time Capsule requires AFP or SMBv1, but Time Machine backups now use the SMBv2 or SMBv3 protocol.

  • AirPort Utility - AirPort Utility is no longer included when you install ‌macOS Golden Gate‌. If you had the app before updating, you can still use it, but Apple makes no guarantee that it still works. AirPort Utility lets users manage AirPort base stations like the AirPort Extreme and AirPort Express.


macOS 28, which is expected in fall 2027, will largely drop support for Rosetta 2. Most apps that rely on Rosetta will not open on Macs running macOS 28, though Apple is making an exception for some legacy games that are unmaintained.

In ‌macOS Golden Gate‌, you'll see a warning when using any app that relies on Rosetta, so you're aware that the app won't continue to work in the future without a developer update. You can also see which apps are affected by going to Settings > General > About > Intel-Based Apps and then clicking on Details.

entry.title: The iPhone Duo’s odd shape actually has a very cool name
entry.content:
Macworld

The upcoming iPhone Duo’s form has widely been referred to as a having a “similar size to a passport,” comparing it to an object most people are familiar with. But an article by British GQ last week points out that the shape is based on the A-size paper format that’s used internationally.

A Macworld Podcast listener provides some specifics:

I wanted to comment on the aspect ratio of the Duo’s outer and inner screens – both about 1.4 : 1. As an ex-graphic designer, this ratio (known as the silver ratio, 1 to the square root of 2) is very well known to me. That is because in the UK and Europe all our paper sizes are based on this ratio. 

A4 is 297 x 210mm which when folded exactly in half results in A5, which has the same ratio. This continues with smaller sizes of A6, etc. Going the other way, A3 is double A4, etc, until you get to A0, which has a surface area of 1 metre squared. Neat eh? 

The iPhone Duo therefore is like an A5 sheet of paper, folded in half when closed, and is something that will have been very familiar with Molly Anderson who (like Jony Ive) is from the UK.  

Stuart G. via email

I don’t know about you, but I prefer referring to the iPhone Duo’s shape as the “silver ratio” instead of “passport style.” It’s catchy and classy. And it’s cool to know that Apple put some serious thought into the form factor and not just arbitrarily picking a shape.

The iPhone Duo was introduced during the “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9. Apple will start taking orders for the iPhone Duo on October 16, and shipments start on October 23. Learn more about the iPhone Duo.

entry.title: Should you buy an Apple Watch now or wait? Best time to buy in 2026
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple’s 2026 Watch lineup is now on sale, with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 joining the Apple Watch SE 3. That makes this a reasonable time to buy if you want the latest features. If price matters more, compare the new models with discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock – or wait for the October and Black Friday sales. The SE 3 remains the least expensive option in Apple’s current lineup, but it’s also the oldest as it was introduced in September 2025.

If you don’t need a watch immediately, it’s worth considering the major sales events that follow Apple’s launch. Retailers consistently offer their biggest Apple Watch discounts during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday in November. During Prime Day in June 2026, for example, we saw discounts ranging from $50 to $120 on current models.

In this guide, we’ll explain whether you should buy an Apple Watch now or wait, the best times of year to find the biggest discounts, and how to avoid paying full price just before a new model arrives. Read our Macworld’s Best Apple Watch guide for more buying advice.

Should I buy an Apple Watch now? At a glance

Buy an Apple Watch now if…

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry

The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale alongside the SE 3 and there are no new models expected. Buy now if you need a watch soon or the model you want meets your needs at a price you’re happy to pay. The Series 12 is the best everyday choice, the SE 3 is the best value, and the Ultra 4 makes sense if you need its longer battery life or outdoor features. A discounted Series 11 or Ultra 3 could also be worth buying if you don’t need the latest additions.

You should consider buying now if:

  • Your current Apple Watch cannot run watchOS 27, or its battery no longer lasts long enough for your needs.
  • You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model. The current watches offer substantial improvements in displays, performance, health tracking and battery life.
  • You want the Series 12 or Ultra 4’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and Readiness score. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026, so don’t count on using those immediately.
  • You would benefit from the Ultra 4’s up to 50-hour battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features.
  • You need a watch before a trip or event, or you find a worthwhile discount on a model that suits you.

Don’t buy an Apple Watch now if…

The main reason to wait now is price: retailers may discount the new models during October sales and Black Friday.

You may want to wait or choose a different model if:

  • You want the lowest possible price and are happy to wait for the next major sale. Compare any Series 12 or Ultra 4 offer with remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock.
  • You already own a Series 10 or 11 and do not need the Series 12’s new health sensing features. Its quoted everyday battery life remains 24 hours.
  • You own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life and outdoor features already meet your needs. The Ultra 4’s 50-hour rating is its clearest reason to upgrade.
  • You are considering a used watch that cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 8, SE 2 and original Ultra, along with older models, miss out on the latest major software update.
  • You use an Android phone. Apple Watch requires an iPhone.
  • You are considering the SE 3 but need ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring or the new Health Sensing System. Choose the Series 12 instead.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best choice for most people. Its new Health Sensing System measures heart rate every five seconds and heart-rate variability more frequently, providing data for a new Readiness score. Outdoor workout tracking lasts longer, however, and a 15-minute charge now provides up to 12 hours of use, compared with around eight hours for Series 11. Aluminum models also gain a tougher Ceramic Shield 2 display. 

Buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:

  • You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model and want the best everyday option.
  • You want the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, and Readiness score.
  • You want advanced features missing from the SE 3, including ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring and hypertension notifications.
  • You prefer a lighter watch with two size choices over the larger Ultra 4.

Don’t buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:

  • You own a Series 10 or 11 that still meets your needs. The new health features may not justify the cost of upgrading, and Apple’s 24-hour everyday battery rating has not changed.
  • You can get a Series 11 at a meaningful discount and don’t need the new health sensing or upcoming Audio Intelligence features.
  • You mainly want fitness tracking, notifications and basic safety features. The SE 3 costs $150/£150 less.
  • You need more than a day of battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features. Consider the Ultra 4 instead.

Our verdict: This is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most people buying a new watch today. Its new health sensing features make it a more substantial upgrade than the Series 11 was, while the starting price has stayed the same. Owners of recent watches should weigh those additions against the cost: a discounted Series 11 – or keeping the watch they already have – may be the better value.

If you don’t need Apple’s most advanced health sensors, the SE 3 delivers almost everything that makes the Apple Watch great at a much lower price. It starts at $249 / £219, although we’ve already seen it discounted to $199 during major sales.

Buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:

Don’t buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:

  • You need ECG or blood oxygen monitoring, which are only available on the Series 12 and Ultra 4.
  • You want the brightest display and most premium design—the SE 3 still has thicker bezels than the flagship models.
  • You need longer battery life. The SE 3 is rated for 18 hours, compared with 24 hours for the Series 12.
  • You’re happy to spend more for Apple’s most advanced health and fitness features.

Our verdict: The Apple Watch SE 3 is an outstanding budget smartwatch. Its always-on display, S10 processor, fast charging and improved health features make it a huge step up from the SE 2. Unless you specifically need ECG, blood oxygen monitoring or the longer battery life of the Series 11, the SE 3 is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most buyers.

It starts at $799/£749, the same starting price as the Ultra 3, and retains the 49mm titanium case, bright display, dual-frequency GPS, satellite communication and diving support. 

Battery life is the strongest reason to choose the new model. Apple rates the Ultra 4 for up to 50 hours of normal use, up from 42 hours on Ultra 3, or 84 hours in Low Power Mode, up from 72. Its new Extended Workout modes can track outdoor activity for up to 25 hours with full GPS and heart-rate readings, or up to 45 hours in Max Extended Workout mode. Like the Series 12, it gains the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and a Readiness score. Its S11 chip supports Audio Intelligence, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026. 

Buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:

  • You want the longest battery life available on an Apple Watch, particularly for travel, long shifts or time away from a charger.
  • You need extended outdoor workout tracking, precision dual-frequency GPS or satellite communication.
  • You hike, dive or take part in endurance sports and will use its rugged case, Action button and specialist features.
  • You want the new Health Sensing System in an Ultra watch and are upgrading from a substantially older model.

Don’t buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:

  • You already own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life meets your needs. It retains many of the same outdoor features, including satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS.
  • You find an Ultra 3 at a substantial discount and do not need the Ultra 4’s longer battery life, new health sensing or extended workout modes.
  • You mainly want advanced health features in an everyday watch. The smaller Series 12 has the same new Health Sensing System and S11 chip for half the starting price.
  • You prefer a smaller or lighter watch. The Ultra 4’s 49mm case can feel bulky, especially for sleep tracking.

Our verdict: The Ultra 4 is worth buying if you will benefit from its 50-hour battery life, extended workout tracking or outdoor safety features. It also offers the Series 12’s new health sensing in a more rugged watch. For everyday use, the Series 12 offers better value; if you already own an Ultra 3, compare the cost of upgrading with how much its extra eight hours of rated battery life and new health features matter to you. 

Should I buy an older Apple Watch?

The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are now the previous-generation models and may be good buys if retailers discount them enough. Before choosing any older Apple Watch, check both its price against the current model and whether it can run watchOS 27. The Series 9 and Ultra 2 are the oldest supported Apple Watch models models in their respective ranges; the SE 3 is the only supported SE.

The following models cannot install watchOS 27, so we would generally avoid buying them unless the price is exceptionally low and you are comfortable using older software:

  • Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
  • Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
  • Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
  • Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)

Start by comparing a discounted Series 11 with the Series 12, or an Ultra 3 with the Ultra 4. The Series 11 retains the Series 12’s 24-hour everyday battery rating but lacks its new Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features. The Ultra 3 retains satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS, but its rated battery life is 42 hours rather than the Ultra 4’s 50 hours. Series 10 and Ultra 2 can offer further savings if their price and battery condition make sense; Series 9 is the oldest standard model that runs watchOS 27.

What to look for when buying an older Apple Watch

  • Choose an S9 chip or newer for the longest software support.
  • Buy refurbished if possible. Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store includes a one-year warranty, while reputable third-party refurbishers can also offer good value.
  • Shop during major sales. Previous-generation Apple Watches often receive their biggest discounts during Prime Day and Black Friday.
  • Check the battery and Activation Lock. If you’re buying used, confirm the battery is in good condition, inspect the watch for damage, and make sure Activation Lock has been removed before you buy.

When is the best time to buy an Apple Watch?

The best time to buy an Apple Watch depends on whether you want the newest model or the lowest price.

The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale, alongside the SE 3. If you want the latest model and are happy with its price, you can buy now without an imminent replacement to worry about. If getting a discount matters more, compare retailers during the expected October sales and Black Friday in November.

The September launch also makes the Series 11 and Ultra 3 worth checking. Retailers may reduce remaining stock, but compare the actual saving with the features you would give up: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 add new health sensing, while the Ultra 4 also increases rated battery life from 42 to 50 hours.

Apple kept the new models’ starting prices at $399/£369 for Series 12 and $799/£749 for Ultra 4. Individual configurations and retailer prices vary.

When shouldn’t you buy an Apple Watch?

Avoid buying an Apple Watch:

  • Just before Apple’s annual September event, unless you need one immediately.
  • At full price when a major sale is only days away, such as Prime Day or Black Friday.
  • Without comparing prices. Check multiple retailers and use price-tracking tools such as CamelCamelCamel to avoid inflated “sale” prices.
  • If you’re paying extra for cellular but don’t need it. Cellular Apple Watch typically cost around $100 more and require a monthly data plan, while the GPS model offers better value for most people.
  • If battery life is your top priority. Apple Watch battery life still trails some competing smartwatches, so you may prefer an alternative platform if multi-day battery life is essential.

Where to find the best Apple Watch deals

Apple rarely discounts the Apple Watch itself, so the best deals are usually found at third-party retailers – we check these every month and record the best deals here: Top Apple Watch discounts & deals – Big savings on all models.

Best places to buy: Amazon is consistently one of the best places to find Apple Watch discounts, particularly during major sales. Other good options in the U.S. include Best Buy, Walmart, Target and Costco. In the U.K., check Amazon, Currys, Argos, John Lewis and KRCS.

Shop during major sales: The biggest discounts typically arrive during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday/Cyber Monday (November). Savings of $100–$150 on current-generation models are common. During Prime Day 2026, for example, the Apple Watch Series 11 fell to $279 ($120 off) and the Ultra 3 dropped to $649 ($150 off).

Check for education discounts: Students, teachers and education staff may qualify for discounted Apple Watch pricing through Apple’s Education Store U.S. (and Education Store U.K.). For more information read our guide to how to get a student discount at the Apple Education Store.

Tip: Before buying, compare prices across several retailers and check the recent price history with a tool such as CamelCamelCamel to make sure you’re getting a genuine deal rather than a temporary “discount” from an inflated price.

Is it worth buying a refurbished Apple Watch?

Buying a refurbished Apple Watch is another great way to save money, provided you buy from a reputable seller and choose a model that will continue to receive software updates.

Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is the safest option. Every watch undergoes rigorous testing, cleaning and inspection, comes with a one-year warranty, includes new accessories, and is eligible for AppleCare. Apart from the plain white box, it’s difficult to tell the difference between a refurbished Apple Watch and a brand-new one. You can typically save around 15% on recent models, with even bigger discounts on older generations.

Check Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store or U.K. Refurbished Store for current models, configurations and prices. Stock changes regularly; compare any refurbished Series 11 or Ultra 3 with the price of a new Series 12 or Ultra 4 before buying.

The best Apple Watch refurbished deals:

Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store often has Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 3, SE 2, Ultra 2 and Ultra 3.

You may also find the Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 2, SE 3 and Ultra 3 at Apple’s U.K. Refurbished Store.

Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for £309, £60 off

Third-party refurbishers can also offer excellent value, but quality varies. Terms such as “Excellent” or “Grade A”aren’t standardised, so always check the seller’s warranty, return policy and battery condition before buying. Be aware that Amazon Renewed devices, for example, aren’t refurbished to Apple’s standards and may not include a new battery or replacement parts.

The other key consideration is software support. Older Apple Watches eventually stop receiving new versions of watchOS, so avoid buying a model that’s nearing the end of its supported life. For the best balance of price and features, compare refurbished Series 11 and Ultra 3 models with the new generation first. Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 can cost less and still run watchOS 27, but check their condition and savings carefully.

A refurbished Apple Watch can be one of the best values in Apple’s lineup – as long as you buy from a trusted seller and don’t choose a model that’s too old.

Read: Should I buy a refurbished Apple Watch? for more information.

FAQ

1.

Should I wait for the next Apple Watch?

You do not need to wait for 2026’s launch: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 went on sale in September 2026, and the SE 3 remains in Apple’s lineup. If you need a watch now, choose the model that fits your needs and budget. If you are mainly looking for a lower price, consider waiting for a sale or comparing discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock.

Apple has not announced when the next Apple Watch models will arrive, but we expect that the next update will happen in September 2027.

2.

How long does Apple support an Apple Watch?

Apple has traditionally supported Apple Watches with major watchOS updates for around five to six years, but that changed with watchOS 27, announced at WWDC 2026.

Apple dropped support for five older models in a single release:

  • Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
  • Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
  • Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
  • Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)

As a result, watchOS 27 only supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, starting with the Apple Watch Series 9. While Apple may continue to provide security updates for older models for a limited time, they no longer receive new watchOS features.

The change makes software support a much more important consideration when buying an older or refurbished Apple Watch. If you want the longest possible lifespan, choose a model with an S9 chip or newer.

3.

Is the Apple Watch Series 11 still worth buying?

If it is substantially cheaper than the Series 12. Both have up to 24 hours of rated everyday battery life, but the Series 12 adds more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, a Readiness score and support for upcoming Audio Intelligence features, so be sure that you are willing to give those features up for the saving.
